result.html:
Inanivutia kuona jinsi Mungu anavyotumia watu Wake katika historia kuleta utukufu kwa Jina Lake. Anatumia vitu dhaifu kuwachanganya wenye hekima; vitu vya chini kuufanya uzingo wa wana watu wenye hekima wa dunia kutokuwa na thamani. Mungu anatumia udhaifu wa mwili, taabu, upotevu, majonzi, bidii, na maumivu kuongeza hazina zetu za kiroho na kujenga Ufalme Wake hapa duniani!

Wimbo huu ukawa wa thamani kwa familia yangu na mimi miaka michache iliyopita tuliposubiri kuzaliwa kwa mtoto wetu wa nne mwenye matatizo ya kijenetiki. Tulijua hangeweza kubaki kwa muda mrefu pamoja nasi. Alikufa akiwa na siku tatu tu. Baada ya kutafiti kuhusu wimbo huu, nilishangaa kugundua kwamba mtu aliyekuwa na hadithi iliyomhamasisha mwimbaji alimtangaza alipoteza watoto nane kati ya tisa wake.

Hadithi ya mtu huyu ni ya kutambulika. Miaka yake 61 duniani yamewekwa alama na majonzi na upotevu, mateso na kifungo. Hata hivyo, kujitolea kwake kwa Kristo kulikuwa kwa kiwango cha juu, na moto wake kwa Mungu na hamu yake ya kuhubiri injili hakukosekana hadi siku yake ya mwisho.

Samuel Rutherford, mwana wa mwanamkulima mwenye mali, alizaliwa mwaka 1600. Maisha yake yalianza katika kijiji kidogo cha Nisbet, Scotland. Tunapoangalia maisha yake, tunagundua mkono wa Mungu ukifanya kazi katika miaka ya mapema ya Samuel. Alipokuwa na miaka mitatu tu, alikuwa akicheza na marafiki zake alipokuwa anakumbwa na kuangukia kisima cha mji. Dada yake na marafiki wakakimbia kupata msaada. Waliporudi, walimpata Samuel akiwa amebeba maji karibu na kisima. Wakamwuliza alivyotoka, na aliposema, "Mtu mweupe mzuri alikuja akaninogoa kutoka kwenye kisima." Familia yake waliamini kwamba Mungu alimpeleka malaika kumwokoa siku hiyo.

Kulingana na tunachojua kuhusu Samuel Rutherford, alikuwa na ndugu wawili na dada mmoja. Alitumwa shule akiwa mdogo, na akawa mwanafunzi mwenye bidii sana. Alijifunza Kilatini na Kigiriki vizuri sana hadi hatimaye akawa profesa. Alioa Eupham Hamilton karibu mwaka 1624, hivi karibuni baada ya kuanza kufundisha katika Chuo Kikuu cha Edinburgh. Wakati huo, Samuel hakuwa bado ameongoka na alizingatia tu kufuatilia malengo yake ya kitaaluma.

Mwaka 1626, akiwa na umri wa miaka 26, Samuel alipata imani wazi na ya kuokolewa kwa Bwana Yesu Kristo. Alisema, "Ee lakini Kristo ana jicho la kuokoa. Alipolitania kwangu mara ya kwanza nilikuokoka. Ilimgharimu tu kuangalia kufanya kuzimu kuninyooshea." Tangu wakati huo alijazwa na shauku ya kuhubiri na kuzungumza kuhusu Mwokozi wake. Mabadiliko haya ya maisha yalisababisha vurugu katika chuo kiasi kwamba Rutherford alimaliza kujiuzulu nafasi yake ya uprofesa.

Mwaka 1627, Samuel alichukua mkewe na watoto wawili wadogo kwenda Galloway, Scotland, ambapo alianza kuwa mchungaji wa kanisa dogo la Anwoth. Alipoanza wito wake pale alisema, "Nimepokea mamlaka kutoka kwa Mwalimu wa kifalme na wa kijinga, Bwana wangu Yesu, kuhubiri Kristo kwa watu." Shauku yake ilikuwa kwa wokovu wa watu, na inasemekana kwamba alionekana kuwa daima anasali, daima anahubiri, daima akitembelea wagonjwa, daima akifundisha na kuelimisha, daima akiandika au akisoma. Waliopaa sana alivyohubiri na hamu yake kwa ustawi wa makanisa yao ilikuwa na athari kubwa kwao. Si wao tu, bali watu waliokuja kutoka miji na vijiji vinavyozunguka kumtukuzwa. Rafiki mmoja aliwahi kuripoti, "Mara nyingi nilifikiria angeweza kuruka kutoka kanisani alipokuwa anazungumzia Yesu Kristo."

Samuel hakuachwa na majonzi na huzuni. Mwaka 1631, miaka minne tu baada ya kuanza kazi yake kama mchungaji, mkewe alifariki. Watoto wake wawili pia wakaugua na kuondoka katika dunia hii. Mwaka 1636, baada ya miaka tisa ya kuhubiri, alitetewa hadi Aberdeen, ambapo aliamriwa kususia kuhubiri injili. Hii ilikuwa wakati mgumu kwake kwani alikosa sana mkewe na watoto pamoja na makanisa yake, Kanisa la Anwoth. Kipindi hiki maishani mwake ni mojawapo ya sababu anavyokumbukwa sana, kwa sababu alianza kuandika barua kwa watu wa kanisa lake na marafiki. Kutoka kwa barua 365 alizoandika, 220 kati yao ziliandikwa katika miezi 22 ya uhamisho huyo.

Serikali hatimaye ilibadilika mikononi, jambo ambalo lilileta uhuru zaidi kwa Wakili wa Agano waliositishwa. Hivyo Rutherford alirudi kwa haraka kwa kundi lake mpendwa Anwoth. Karibu mwaka mmoja baadaye, msimu wa vuli wa 1639, aliondoka tena Anwoth kwa kukasirika lakini wakati huu ili kutimiza uteuzi wa kuwa Profesa wa Ustaarabu katika St Mary's College huko St. Andrews. Mabadiliko haya yalikuwa magumu kwake, kwani tena alikosa sana makanisa yake. Anaandika, "Kuondoka kwangu kutoka kundi langu ni mzito sana kwangu, kiasi kwamba kunawafanya maisha yangu kuwa mzigo, sikuwahi kuwa na hamu kama hiyo ya kifo. Bwana anisaidie na kuimarisha mchanga huyu wa huzuni."

Baada ya miezi mitano katika nafasi yake mpya na akiwa peke yake kwa karibu miongo miwili, Samuel mwenye umri wa miaka 40 alioa Jean McMath. Pamoja walizaa watoto saba. Kwa masikitiko, sita kati yao walikufa utotoni na enzi za utoto. Ni binti mmoja aliyeitwa Agnes aliyebaki hadi ukuaji.

Rutherford aliendelea kuwa kiongozi mwenye ushawishi katika harakati za wasiobadilika nchini Scotland kwa miaka 20 iliyofuata hadi 1660. Kwa kifo cha Cromwell, utawala wa taifa lilikuja mwisho, na Charles II akarudishwa madarakani. Mara nyingine tena, hasira za kifalme zilimpata Samuel. Alitumwa kuonekana mbele ya jaji na kumshtaki kwa uhaini dhidi ya serikali kwa kuhubiri kweli. Alitumwa gerezani kusubiri kutekelezwa adhabu. Hata hivyo, kabla mfalme angeweza kumtii, Samuel aliuma sana. Alisema, "Nina wito tayari kutoka Jaji wa juu, na ni lazima nijibu wito wangu wa kwanza na wakati siku yako itafika nitakuwa mahali ambapo wafalme wachache na watu wakubwa huja."

Aliproga saa za jioni za siku yake ya mwisho, akijibu swali, "Mnadhani sasa nini kuhusu Kristo?" akajibu hivi, "Ee, wajua ndugu zangu wote katika nchi ni Mwanafunzi aliemwongoza nani nimehudumu kwake, na amani gani nina leo! Nitalala katika Kristo, na nitakapomwake nitafurahishwa kwa sura Yake. Usiku huu utaifunga mlango, na kuiweka nanga yangu ndani ya pazia, nami nitaondoka kwa usingizi saa tano asubuhi. Utukufu! utukufu kwa Muumba wangu na Mwokozi wangu milele! Nitaishi na kumwabudu. Ee, kwa mikono ya kumkumbatia! Ee, kwa kibao kilichopangwa vizuri! Utukufu! utukufu unaishi katika nchi ya Immanuel!" Maneno haya yaliwasikika na mkewe, binti na marafiki, na alikuwa pamoja na Mwanaweza kwake saa tano asubuhi.

Karibu karne mbili baadaye, Annie Ross Cousin, mshairi wa Scotland na mwandishi wa nyimbo na mke wa mchungaji, alihamasishwa na maisha na maandishi ya Samuel Rutherford. Aliandika muhtasari wa maisha yake katika wimbo wa kumbukumbu, "The Sands of Time are Sinking". Wimbo huu ulitolewa mara ya kwanza mwaka 1857 katika Christian Treasury. Kutoka kwa vifungu asilia kumi na tisa, vinne tu vinatumika katika vitabu vya nyimbo zetu. (kwa nakala iliyo kwa herufi nzito)

The sands of time are sinking,
The dawn of heaven breaks,
The summer morn I’ve sighed for,
The fair, sweet morn awakes:
Dark, dark hath been the midnight,
But dayspring is at hand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

2. Oh! well it is forever,
Oh! well forevermore
My nest hung in no forest
Of all this death-doomed shore!
Yea, let the vain world vanish,
As from the ship the stand,
While glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

3. There the Red Rose of Sharon
Unfolds its heart-most bloom.
And fills the air of Heaven
With ravishing perfume;
Oh, to behold its blossom,
While by its fragrance fann’d
Where glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

4. The King there in His beauty,
Without a veil is seen:
It were a well-spent journey
Though seven deaths lay between:
The Lamb with His fair army,
Doth on Mount Zion stand;
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

5. Oh! Christ He is the fountain,
The deep sweet well of Love!
The streams on earth I’ve tasted,
More deep I’ll drink above;
There, to an ocean fullness,
His mercy doth expand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

6. E’en Anwoth was not heaven—
E’en preaching was not Christ;
And in my sea-beat prison
My Lord and I held tryst:
And aye my murkiest storm-cloud
Was by a rainbow spann’d,
Caught from the glory dwelling
In Immanuel’s land.

7. But that He built a heaven
Of His surpassing love,
A little New Jerus’lem,
Like to the one above,—
“Lord, take me o’er the water,”
Had been my loud demand,
“Take me to love’s own country,
Unto Immanuel’s land.”

8. But flowers need night’s cool darkness,
The moonlight and the dew;
So Christ, from one who loved it,
His shining oft withdrew;
And then, for cause of absence,
My troubled soul I scann’d—
But glory, shadeless, shineth
In Immanuel’s land.

9. The little birds of Anwoth,
used to count them blest,—
Now, beside happier alters,
go to built my nest:
O’er these there broods no silence,
No graves around them stand,
For glory, deathless, dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

10. Fair Anwoth by the Solway,
To me thou still art dear!
E’en from the verge of Heaven
I drop for thee a tear.
Oh! if one soul from Anwoth
Meet me at God’s right hand,
My Heaven will be two Heavens,
In Immanuel’s land!

11. I’ve wrestled on towards Heaven,
‘Ganst storm, and wind, and tide;—
Now, like a weary traveler,
That leaneth on his guide,
Amid the shades of evening,
While sinks life’s ling’ring sand,
I hail the glory dawning
From Immanuel’s land.

12. Deep waters cross’d life’s pathway,
The hedge of thorns was sharp;
Now these lie all behind me,—
Oh, for a well-tuned harp!
Oh, to join Hallelujah
With yon triumphant band,
Who sing where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land!

13. With mercy and with judgment
My web of time He wove,
And aye the dews of sorrow
Were lustered with His love!
I’ll bless the hand that guided,
I’ll bless the heart that plann’d,
When throned where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

14. Soon shall the cup of glory
Wash down earth’s bitterest woes,
Soon shall the desert brier
Break into Eden’s rose:
The curse shall change to blessing–
The name on earth that’s bann’d,
Be graven on the white stone
In Immanuel’s land.

15. Oh! I am my Beloved’s,
And my Beloved’s mine!
He brings a poor vile sinner
Into His “house of wine:”
I stand upon His merit,
I know no other stand,
Not e’en where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

16. I shall sleep sound in Jesus,
Fill’d with His likeness rise,
To live and to adore Him,
To see Him with these eyes:
‘Tween me and resurrection
But Paradise doth stand;
Then—then for glory dwelling
In Immanuel’s land!

17. The bride eyes not her garment,
But her dear Bridegroom’s face;
I will not gaze at glory,
But on my King of Grace—
Not at the crown He giveth,
But on His pierced hand:
The Lamb is all the glory
Of Immanuel’s land.

18. I have borne scorn and hatred,
I have borne wrong and shame,
Earth’s proud ones have reproach’d me,
For Christ’s thrice blessed name:
Where God His seal set fairest
They’ve stamp’d their foulest brand;
But judgment shines like noonday
In Immanuel’s land.

19. They’ve summoned me before them,
But there I may not come,—
My Lord says, “Come up hither,”
My Lord says, “Welcome home!
My King now at His white throne,
My presence doth command,
Where glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

Tune nzuri inayolingana vizuri na maandishi haya ilitengenezwa mwanzoni mwa 1800 na mwanamuziki Mfaransa, Chretien D`Urhan. Inafaa vizuri kwa maneno ya wimbo—tembo yake ya hamsini inalingana na uzito wa maneno. Mstari wa melodi unaopanda katika kifungu cha mwisho unalingana kikamilifu na furaha inayotarajiwa iliyoonyeshwa na kifungu cha kurudia—"And glory, glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land."

Tunapo maliza historia ya wimbo huu, tuendelee kushangazwa na uenyeuzi wa Mungu katika maisha ya wale walio mbele yetu. Tufuate Kristo kwa mioyo yetu yote na tuwe vyombo vinavyotayarika kwa matumizi ya Mwalimu! Nukuu moja ya mwisho kutoka kwa Samuel Rutherford tuichukue pamoja nasi. "They lose nothing who gain Christ."

Taarifa kwa ajili ya makala hii ilichukuliwa kutoka 101 Hymn Stories, A Treasury of Hymns, Crichbaptist.org.
